note: Frozen evaluation set, append-only on the same terms as questions.json: add questions, never reword one, because a reworded question silently invalidates every earlier recording that used it (D-088).
why: D-094 measured max_depth 0 vs 1 vs 2 on the broad set and found no quality difference at 2.8x the retrieval. But every question in that set is a single-area survey prompt ('what is attention?'), which is the case least likely to need decomposition -- so the null result may be a property of the questions, not of recursion. These questions are built to be the opposite: each one is an INTERSECTION of two or three areas that the broad set covers separately, so a single arXiv query cannot cover it and a planner that decomposes well should win. Deliberately drawn from the same subject areas as questions.json, so a difference cannot be explained away as 'arXiv has fewer papers on these topics'.
falsifies: If depth shows no gain here either, recursive decomposition is decoration on this workload and the thesis should say so (O-14).
